To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of a calmodulin-spectrum complex provides a molecular basis for the understanding of the regulation of membrane plasticity and cell integrity.

we have solved the structure of a complex formed by the calmodulin binding domain of αII-spectrum and calmodulin and that this complex is hydrophobic, and the spectrin binding site is an amphiphilc helix.

calmodulin binds to a hydrophobic region of spectrin, that this interaction is required to activate calpain and caspase proteases that cleave spectrin, and that phosphorylation of spectrin by Src kinase inhibits this interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the cytoskeleton.
the molecular basis of the interaction between calmodulin and αII-specterin, and how this interaction regulates membrane plasticity.
the regulation of cell plasticity and integrity through the interaction of calmodulin with the cytoskeletal protein, αII-specterin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calmodulin-spectrum complex is an excellent example of a protein that has been designed for regulation of cellular plasticity.
the crystal structure of the complex of calmodulin and αII-spectrain provides a basis for understanding the regulation of cell plasticity by calmodulin.
calmodulin binds to the spectrin repeat unit 11 and the calmodulation of spectrin is a mechanism of cell plasticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calmodulin binds to an unstructured region within spectrin and that the binding event induces a helical conformation that is susceptible to cleavage by calpain and other proteases.
calmodulin is the master regulator of membrane plasticity.
calmodulin binds to a hydrophobic surface of the spectrin domain, and the spectrin domain folds into a helix once it is bound to calmodulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

calmodulin binds to the unstructured insert of spectrin in the 11(1) repeat of αII-spectrum in the same way it binds to the C-terminal helix of myosin light chain kinase, but with the addition of a second calmodulin molecule that binds to the N-terminal end of the spectrin insert.
calmodulin binds to the calmodulin binding domain of αII-Spectin in a hydrophobic manner.
the calmodulin-spectrum complex is a hydrophobic interaction between two amphiphilic molecules.
